title: "Thermal envelope and heat flows"
---

{{< include _includes/preset-help-envelope.qmd >}}

::: {.lead}
Two thermally decoupled model zones
:::

The model distinguishes an **actively cooled zone and a zone without active cooling, thermally decoupled from one another**.[^rc-modell]

Solar gains enter through windows; internal heat gains arise inside the room.

![Thermal energy model with two thermally decoupled zones, heat flows and example balances.](../illustrations/thermisches_modell.svg){.manual-figure}

::: {.callout-warning title="Caution"}
[LCA](climate.qmd) also includes constructions inside and outside the thermal boundary. Thermal envelope area and component quantities recorded for LCA are not interchangeable.
:::

## Entering building-physics inputs {#excel-bauphysik}

Describe the areas and properties of components that determine the district's heat exchange.

::: {.excel-operation}
**Where in PEXL?** Open [🧱]{.excel-menu .darkred} **Bauphysik** (building physics).
:::

### Inputs on the building-physics sheet

| Input group | Assignment |
|---|---|
| Opaque thermal envelope | External walls excluding windows, roof or uppermost thermal ceiling, basement ceiling/ground-contact floor; areas and U-values |
| Translucent components | Window areas including frames by orientation, U-values and g-values |
| Thermal bridges / airtightness | Allowance and n50 assumption based on project information |
| Shading / movable solar protection | Reduction factors and control assumptions; distinguish suggested values from values actually applied |
| Effective thermal mass | Construction type and effective heat capacity |

Apply [presets](presets.qmd), then check project-specific areas and properties. After calculation, check the heat balance on the [results sheet](results.qmd#waermebilanz).

::: {.declaration-note}
**Declaration:** Internal heat gains and user electricity can in principle be modelled freely. For a declaration, use the designated values of the tool version in use.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse=true title="Research / Expert"}
**Combining different component areas:** Inputs are aggregated by component group and orientation. Add only areas with the same boundary condition. For U-values, use $U_\mathrm{eq}=\sum_i A_i U_i/\sum_i A_i$, preserving the transmission conductance $\sum_i A_i U_i$.

Worked example: 100 m² of wall at 0.20 W/(m² K) and 50 m² at 0.40 W/(m² K) give 150 m² at approximately 0.267 W/(m² K). Treat windows and opaque walls separately.

Window U-values refer to the whole window including the frame; g-values refer to glazing. Weight g-values by glazing area and account for frame fractions and shading separately. Do not combine orientations. This simplification assumes comparable solar exposure and boundary conditions; document component areas and assumptions.
:::

[^rc-modell]: According to the project team, the thermal calculation follows the simplified dynamic approach of ÖNORM B 8110-6. This identifies the methodological basis, not a claim of full compliance with the standard. Each zone uses a simplified thermal RC model with one thermal mass: heat capacity C represents storage, and resistances R represent heat exchange. No heat exchange is assumed between the two zones. The model supports energy concept assessment; it is not a detailed multi-zone room model. Explanation by the project team; [PEXL training, slides 11–14](../downloads/schulung.pdf) (German).
